owner.occupation: Specialty coffee roaster and café owner in Mangwon-dong

world.bio: Korean-American, grew up in Fullerton, moved back to Seoul to roast coffee. I run a small café and roastery in Mangwon-dong on a secondhand 5kg drum roaster, obsessive about roast curves, quietly bored with coffee lately. Mother is recovering from knee surgery in Incheon. Getting into film photography with a borrowed Pentax. Fighting with the building over a leaking AC unit above the roastery.
skills_assets: Q-grader certified, eight years in specialty coffee, five of them roasting
A secondhand 5kg drum roaster with Artisan logging; roast curve library of about 200 batches
A café with eleven seats, espresso machine, a pour-over bar and a small retail wall of beans
A social following of about 4,800 on Instagram and a mailing list of 600
Wholesale to six cafés in Mapo and Yeonnam
Good bilingual skills in English and Korean, and basic Japanese

projects.name: Evening menu experiment
projects.text: After 7pm half the customers order decaf or nothing, and I hate the decaf I buy: flat, papery. I've been experimenting at night with re-roasting barley and hojicha on the drum roaster to build an evening menu: roasted barley tea lattes, hojicha affogato, a chilled roasted grain drink. Tried 40 test batches so far, and my roast notes for the 'lighter' barley are the best part. The problem: I roast grain on the same machine as the coffee, so the drum smells of toast for a day.

projects.name: Film photography
projects.text: Borrowed a Pentax K1000 from my friend Minho. Shooting Kodak Gold 200 around Mangwon market. Developed three rolls, 14 frames usable.

projects.name: AC leak dispute
projects.text: A condenser unit from the apartment above drips onto the roastery ceiling. Third official notice to the building owner, no response. Lost two bags of green beans to moisture already.

notes.text: Roasted a Kenyan Nyeri AA, 210 degrees, first crack at 8:48. Beautiful. But I noticed I was bored halfway through. I wonder what that means. I used to rush to the roaster.
Evening shift: eleven customers after 7, six decafs, three nothing, two ordering regular. One said 'I can't sleep if I have coffee'. I understand but hate the decaf we sell. It tastes like cardboard.
Re-roasted barley at 190 degrees for 11 minutes. Smell: toasted cereal, toffee, a bit like Hoppang. Brewed it like coffee: very nutty, somewhat sweet. Customers at the bar liked it.
Mum phoned from Incheon, knee still sore. Said 'don't come this weekend, you're busy'. I know that means come this weekend.
Hojicha trial: 160 degrees, 6 minutes. Too smoky above 170. The sweet spot is narrow. It's like a light coffee roast, honestly. Logged curves in Artisan.
AC leak, again. Called the landlord, got voicemail. Put a bucket under it. It's almost comforting, the plink plink.
Developed a roll. Most frames blurry. One frame of my barista Ji-won laughing, perfect. Printed it, stuck it next to the register.
Wholesale customer asked for a new decaf. I said I'm not satisfied with my decaf. He said 'whatever you give me is fine.' It isn't.

messages.text: Minho: How's the Pentax? Me: Blurry. Minho: It's manual focus. Me: I'm aware. Minho: Use f/8 and zone focus. Me: Fine.
Mum: Eat properly. Me: I am. Mum: You roast all day, you don't eat. Me: I eat a lot of toast. Mum: That's not food.
Ji-won: Customers keep asking if we have anything non-coffee at night. Me: Working on it. Ji-won: The barley thing? Me: Yes. Ji-won: Smells like my grandma's kitchen. Me: Good or bad? Ji-won: Good.
Landlord: Mr. Park, I'll look into the AC. Me: It's been three weeks. Landlord: I'll look into it. Me: Thank you.

calendar.event: Meeting with building owner about AC

relations.about: Lives in Incheon, recovering from knee surgery, proud but worried.

constraints: Roaster is single-drum; can't roast grains and coffee on the same day without cleaning
sensitive: Doubts whether he still loves coffee
Café margins are thin, he pays himself little
Feels guilty about being far from his mother
